verses.text: Saul was still breathing threats and murder against the Lord’s disciples. He went to the high priest
and asked for letters to the synagogues in Damascus. If he found anyone belonging to the Way—man or woman—he planned to arrest them and bring them bound to Jerusalem.
As he traveled and got close to Damascus, a light from heaven suddenly flashed around him.
He fell to the ground and heard a voice say, “Saul, Saul, why are you persecuting me?”
He asked, “Who are you, Lord?” The voice answered, “I am Jesus, the one you are persecuting.
Get up, go into the city, and you’ll be told what you need to do.”
The men traveling with Saul stood there speechless. They heard the sound, but saw no one.
Saul got up from the ground. When he opened his eyes, he couldn’t see anything. They took him by the hand and led him into Damascus.
For three days he couldn’t see, and he neither ate nor drank.
There was a disciple in Damascus named Ananias. The Lord called to him in a vision, “Ananias!” He answered, “I’m here, Lord.”
The Lord told him, “Get up and go to the street called Straight. At the house of Judas, ask for a man from Tarsus named Saul. He is praying right now.
In a vision, he has seen a man named Ananias come in and lay hands on him so he can see again.”
Ananias answered, “Lord, I’ve heard from many people how much harm this man has done to your holy people in Jerusalem.
And he has authority from the chief priests to arrest everyone who calls on your name.”
But the Lord said, “Go. I have chosen him as my instrument to carry my name to the nations, to their kings, and to the people of Israel.
I will show him how much he must suffer for my name.”

So Ananias went to the house and laid his hands on Saul. He said, “Brother Saul, the Lord Jesus, who appeared to you on the road as you came here, sent me so you can see again and be filled with the Holy Spirit.”
At once, something like scales fell from Saul’s eyes, and he could see again. He got up and was baptized.
After eating, he regained his strength. Saul stayed several days with the disciples in Damascus.
Right away, he began proclaiming in the synagogues that Jesus is the Son of God.

Everyone who heard him was amazed. “Isn’t this the man who caused chaos for those who called on Jesus’ name in Jerusalem?” they asked. “Didn’t he come here to arrest them and take them to the chief priests?”
But Saul grew stronger and baffled the Jewish people living in Damascus as he proved that Jesus is the Messiah.
After many days, they plotted together to kill him.
Saul learned about their plan. They watched the city gates day and night, ready to kill him.
But his disciples took him at night and lowered him in a basket through an opening in the city wall.
When Saul arrived in Jerusalem, he tried to join the disciples. They were all afraid of him and didn’t believe he was a disciple.
But Barnabas took him to the apostles and explained how Saul had seen the Lord on the road, how the Lord had spoken to him, and how Saul had boldly preached in Jesus’ name in Damascus.
Saul stayed with them, coming and going around Jerusalem.
He spoke boldly in the name of the Lord Jesus and debated with the Greek-speaking Jews. They tried to kill him.
When the believers found out, they took him down to Caesarea and sent him off to Tarsus.
Then the church throughout Judea, Galilee, and Samaria had peace and grew stronger. Living in reverence for the Lord and receiving the Holy Spirit’s encouragement, it kept growing.
As Peter traveled through the region, he also visited the believers living in Lydda.
There he found a man named Aeneas who had been bedridden for eight years because he was paralyzed.
Peter said to him, “Aeneas, Jesus Christ heals you. Get up and make your bed!” Immediately, Aeneas got up.
Everyone living in Lydda and Sharon saw him and turned to the Lord.
In Joppa there was a disciple named Tabitha, which in Greek means Dorcas. She was always doing good and helping people in need.
Around that time she became sick and died. After washing her body, they laid her in an upstairs room.
Since Lydda was near Joppa, the disciples heard Peter was there and sent two men to him. They urged him, “Please come to us right away.”

Peter got up and went with them. When he arrived, they took him to the upstairs room. All the widows stood beside him crying and showing the robes and other clothes Dorcas had made while she was with them.
Peter sent everyone outside, knelt down, and prayed. Then he turned to the body and said, “Tabitha, get up!” She opened her eyes, saw Peter, and sat up.
He gave her his hand and helped her stand. Then he called the believers and the widows and presented her alive.
The news spread throughout Joppa, and many people believed in the Lord.
Peter stayed in Joppa for many days with a tanner named Simon.
